title: compact-activation-slices-on-demand-scratch-and-kv-shadow-snapshots
author: Ava Martinez
description: Motivation: Peak GPU working set is a persistent cost for high-latency workloads and long-context generation. This PR introduces a combination of "slice compaction" for activations, on-demand scratch allocation for per-kernel temporary buffers, and lightweight KV shadow snapshots to reduce full-checkpoint pressure. The changes are focused on lowering transient workspace requirements without changing model numerics or rollout semantics. Scope: 1) Activation slice compactor: split large activation buffers into smaller addressable slices that are lazily merged/evicted so only hot spans remain resident; 2) On-demand scratch allocator: move from eager per-stream scratch preallocation to a compact pool with per-kernel lazy reservations and reuse heuristics; 3) KV shadow snapshots: a copy-on-write lite snapshot that allows roll-forward without materializing full KV checkpoints; 4) Small scheduler lookahead (2 steps) that co-schedules slices to reduce simultaneous live set peak; 5) Kernel workspace coalescing hints so fused kernels request shared scratch where possible. Benchmarks: Microbench on A100-80GB with GPT-like 30B model lineage and mixed sequence lengths. Typical results vs main (no opt): peak GPU memory reduced 20-28% for gen-time workloads and 14-18% for short-chat workloads; kernel scratch footprint reduced up to 60% for attention-heavy kernels; end-to-end throughput change within ±3%; 99th percentile latency improved 10-12% under steady load due to lower GC/evict spikes. Safety/compatibility: Numeric outputs are byte-for-byte identical for deterministic evals; fallback path remains for architectures that do not support slice addressing. Testing: unit tests for allocator invariants, deterministic replay for KV snapshot, integration perf regression harness runs. Rollout plan: staged rollout behind a feature-flag with an opt-in per-deployment config, initial pilot on Dedicated pool C. Related: ENG-3491 (memory reduction spike), ENG-3512 (kv fallback work). Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked - [x] Microbench harness updated - [x] Unit and integration tests - [x] Feature flag + config - [x] Observability metrics (slice residency, scratch reuse rate) Changeset summary: see commits.

review_comments: Liam Chen: Nice design, but can the slice compactor cause extra memcpy overhead under pathological patterns? Please add telemetry to measure compaction cost and a break-even heuristic.
Author(Ava Martinez): Added compaction cost counters and a simple threshold heuristic; added a unit test simulating pathological interleaved reads to validate the heuristic.
Priya Shah: KV shadow snapshots look promising; ensure we don't double-count memory when snapshots are small. Also add a clear fallback for older Dedicated nodes.
Author: KV shadow snapshots use a weak-ref table to avoid double accounting; fallback path added and covered in integration tests.
Diego Alvarez: CI flaked on scheduler unit test, looks like a timing assumption. Please stabilize the test.
Author: Reworked the scheduler test to use deterministic tick simulation; CI is green now.
release_notes: Reduce peak GPU memory and transient workspace via activation slice compaction, on-demand scratch allocation, and lightweight KV shadow snapshots. Default disabled behind feature flag; rollout planned for Dedicated pilot.
notes: This PR targets production memory pressure reduction with minimal numeric risk; follow-up work will add adaptive slice sizing and per-model profiles for stronger gains.
